COIN.thesis_one_line: America's biggest crypto exchange is gaining share and growing stablecoin income, but profits have collapsed with crypto trading and the price still assumes a full recovery.
kill_criteria: Subscription and services revenue below $500M (low end of Q3'26 outlook) in any quarter through Q2'27.
Adjusted EBITDA negative in any quarter (company's stated commitment: positive Adjusted EBITDA in all market conditions; Q2'26 was $208M).
Average USDC held in Coinbase products below $15B for two consecutive quarters (Q2'26 ATH $20B) or the Circle collaboration terms are cut.
Coinbase Crypto Trading Volume Market Share below 8% for two consecutive quarters (Q2'26 ATH 10.3%).
Corporate cash and cash equivalents below $6.0B (consolidated; Q2'26 $8.6B) with no matching debt repayment.
key_adverse_facts: Q3'26 outlook (8-K 2026-07-30): transaction revenue only ~$130M through 26 July versus $599M for all of Q2; S&S outlook $500-$580M.
Q2'26 subscription and services revenue of $555M was below the low end of the May outlook ($565-$645M); first miss in the five quarters reviewed.
GAAP operating loss $113.5M in Q2'26 (-9.3% margin); Adjusted EBITDA fell from $801M (Q3'25) to $208M (Q2'26); net loss $359.5M.
Executive turnover: Chief Legal Officer left 31 Jul 2026, Chief People Officer 17 Aug 2026; 14% headcount cut and $52.4M restructuring in Q2'26.
Underwood securities-law class action survives for a subset of transactions after the 2026-07-30 summary judgment; state staking actions unresolved.
data_conflicts: Triage cited a $359.5M net loss and revenue -19% y/y (confirmed: total revenue -18.5%, net revenue -17%), but described the loss as operating weakness; $209.5M (Q2) and $691.9M (H1) of it are crypto-investment mark-to-market losses, while the operating loss itself is $113.5M.

Triage said 'third consecutive earnings miss'; the 10-K/10-Q do not report consensus, so that claim is unverified from primary sources (primary-source fact: S&S missed its own outlook once, in Q2'26).

Cash-flow presentation was changed in Q1'26 (payment stablecoins as cash equivalents, loan collateral netted): H1'25 CFO restated from $146M to $1,093M, so TTM FCF cannot be computed on one basis; FY25 CFO as filed was $2,426M.
b1 market cap uses ~264M basic shares ($51.5B); fully diluted shares are ~285M ($55.7B) because of 18.6M options at $26.35 strike and 5.6M RSUs.
COIN.confidence_in_thesis: medium - the primary-source evidence on share gains, balance sheet ($8.6B cash vs $6.0B debt) and the Q3 profit trough is solid, but the 3-year profit path depends on crypto prices I cannot forecast

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for COIN. Reverse DCF at $195.11 (EV $50.6B, F0 $0.9B mid-cycle owner earnings, r 10%, terminal 3.5%) implies 20.4% a year FCF growth for 10 years versus my 12.8% base and 18.7% bull; implied equals base only near $110-120.

COIN.scenario_basis: Start price $195.11 (FY26 EPS negative; consensus FY29 EPS $7.3 as cross-check); 2029E EPS $2.5/$5.3/$7.9; exit P/E 26x/32x/40x; no dividend; probability weights 30/50/20 give about -4% a year.

CVNA.thesis_one_line: The fastest-growing, most profitable US used-car seller keeps taking share, but the shares already price about twenty percent annual cash-flow growth for ten years.
kill_criteria: Retail unit growth below 25% y/y in any quarter (Q2'26 +38%).
Total GAAP gross profit per retail unit below $6,000 for two consecutive quarters (Q2'26 $7,014; Q4'25 $6,427).
Full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance cut below the $2.7B low end, or quarterly Adjusted EBITDA below $600M in Q3 or Q4 2026 (Q2'26 $769M).
Net debt (consolidated debt principal less cash) above 2.0x TTM Adjusted EBITDA (Q2'26 ~0.97x), or any quarter in which finance-receivable sales are completed at a net loss.
Ally master purchase and sale agreement ($8.0B commitment to 2027-07-26) not renewed on substantially similar terms by July 2027.
key_adverse_facts: Gain on loan sales was $349M in Q2'26 ($703M H1): 25% of gross profit and 51% of operating income (10-Q Note 7).

DriveTime (Garcia-controlled) vehicle-service-contract commissions were $113M in Q2'26: 8% of gross profit, 17% of operating income; Garcia Parties control a majority of voting power and a $2.13B tax receivable agreement liability exists (10-Q Note 6).

The first numeric FY26 range ($2.7-3.0B Adjusted EBITDA) implies H2 of $1,259-1,559M versus H1 $1,441M, and press reports it was below sell-side expectations; Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 10.4% from 12.4%.
Cash conversion is weak: TTM FCF $929M versus TTM net income $2,132M (which includes a ~$685M one-off tax benefit); inventory rose $833M in H1'26.
In re Carvana Securities Litigation (D. Ariz.): class-certification motion filed 6 Apr 2026, undecided; legal accrual only $10M.
data_conflicts: Triage said 'FY guidance cut' in Q2 2026; the 8-K of 2026-07-29 gave the FIRST numeric 2026 range ($2.7-3.0B vs $2.24B in 2025); the Q4'25 and Q1'26 releases gave only qualitative 'significant growth'. 'Cut' is versus sell-side expectations only.
Triage FCF yield 0.6% and 31x NTM P/E; primary sources give TTM FCF $929M = 1.3% of $73.3B market cap and ~45x 2026E fully-taxed EPS (~38x on the current low reported tax rate).
Triage cited a Hindenburg report and an Executive Chairman felony conviction; neither appears in the 10-K/10-Q text searched, so both are unverified here.

5-for-1 split on 2026-05-08: pre-split per-share figures (Q1'26 diluted EPS $1.69) equal $0.34 post-split; b1 price $65.06 is post-split. Market cap must use ~1.127B fully-converted shares (718.98M Class A + LLC units), not Class A alone.
CVNA.confidence_in_thesis: medium - four-for-four delivery against guidance and record results are verified, but my base case needs ~2.3M units and 10.5% EBITDA margin by 2036 and half of operating income rests on loan-sale gains

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for CVNA. Reverse DCF at $65.06 (EV $75.8B, F0 $1.3B, r 10%, terminal 3.5%) implies 20.9% a year FCF growth versus my 19.5% base (marginally above); implied equals base at about $58. Probability-weighted value ~$68. [DV11 2026-10-09: r = 10% is unanchored; with 5.17% + Blume beta 2.67 x 4.14% = 16.2% the same model implies 34.2% a year (19.1% at a beta of 1); the 19.5% base is worth $58.5 at 10% and $23.6 at 16.2%. implied_vs_base stays above, more strongly. Verdict and scenario returns unchanged.]

CVNA.scenario_basis: Start price $65.06 (2026E fully-taxed EPS ~$1.45, Adj. EBITDA guide midpoint $2.85B); 2029E EPS $1.8/$3.1/$4.2 on ~1.16B fully-converted shares; exit P/E 16x/26x/30x; no dividend.

FDXF.thesis_one_line: America's biggest less-than-truckload freight carrier, newly spun out of FedEx, earns weak margins in a soft market; it needs a freight recovery to justify today's price.
kill_criteria: Consolidated total leverage ratio (credit-facility definition) above 3.50x at any quarter-end from January 2027, or debt-only net debt/adjusted EBITDA above 3.0x (now ~2.8x).
Adjusted operating margin below 11.0% for any quarter or for the 7-month transition period (guide 11.5-12.0%).
Transition-period adjusted operating income below $605M (low end of guide) when reported, or a guidance cut.
Average daily shipments down more than 6% y/y for two consecutive reporting periods (Mar-May 2026: -5.9%).
FedEx sells its remaining 29.75M shares at more than a 5% discount to the prior close, or the regular dividend is not declared by 30 Jun 2027.
key_adverse_facts: Average daily shipments fell 5.9% y/y in Mar-May 2026 and 4.4% in Q4 CY2025; the 10-K cites 'excess capacity in the LTL industry'.
Fiscal 2026 (to 31 May 2026) carve-out operating income $540M vs $1,404M; adjusted for $492M separation costs 11.7% vs 15.8% margin (-410 bps).
Spin-off debt of $4.3B principal ($4,527M incl. finance leases); credit-facility leverage covenant steps down from 3.75x to 3.50x for quarters ending seven months after the spin; equity is -$497M.
FedEx retains 19.9% (29.75M shares, ~$3.4B) and must dispose of it within 24 months: share-price overhang.
FY26 operating cash flow only $167M and FCF -$212M after reacquiring ~$1.0B of receivables from FedEx's factoring programme; bad-debt provision $91M vs $19M.
data_conflicts: Triage said net debt/EBITDA 6.2x; from the 10-K, debt-only net debt $4,312M / FY26 adjusted EBITDA $1,544M = 2.8x (3.4x with operating leases; 5.8x on GAAP EBITDA including leases).

Triage said negative FCF yield (-3%) and 'no trading history'; confirmed FY26 FCF -$212M, but it is a one-off receivable re-acquisition effect, and normalized FCF is ~$0.75B. Trading history exists since 2026-06-01.
Release of 2026-06-25 reports FY26 operating income $616M / adjusted $1,108M (FedEx segment basis) versus 10-K carve-out $540M / $1,032M; I used the 10-K.

Reported EPS (CY25 $7.08, FY26 $4.38) includes ~$350-390M a year of related-party interest income from FedEx that ends at the spin, so history overstates stand-alone EPS; guidance-based 7-month EPS is $1.75-1.95 (GAAP before MTM).
FDXF.confidence_in_thesis: low-medium - no post-spin quarter has been reported; guidance, the 10-K and the recast history are verified, but stand-alone cost and margin recovery are unproven

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for FDXF. Reverse DCF at $113.18 (EV $21.2B, F0 $0.75B, r 9%, terminal 3%) implies 9.5% a year FCF growth versus my 7.4% base (margin 11.8% to 15.6%); implied equals base near $92; with a mid-cycle F0 of $1.0B it falls to 5.8%, so this is partly a cycle-timing call.

FDXF.scenario_basis: Start price $113.18; 2029E EPS $4.4/$6.0/$7.0 (adjusted operating margin 11.5%/13.7%/15.0% on revenue $9.7B/$10.5B/$11.0B, interest ~$230M, tax 26%, 149.5M shares); exit P/E 15x/22x/25x; assumed cumulative dividends $2/$3/$3 (none declared as of 2026-08-05).
